## Overview

Enable best-effort NUMA binding by default for eligible GPU multiprocessing launches, including PCP. Automatic mode prefers GPU-local memory; explicit binding retains its strict memory policy.

This continues [ivanium/vllm#53](https://github.com/ivanium/vllm/pull/53) by Yifan Qiao (@ivanium). His original commit `788505bea2c6cae925fce4afe47195188656896d` was cherry-picked with authorship, co-author trailers, and sign-offs preserved. The branch includes the merged shared GPU-indexing fix [#61237](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61237) and the CI bot's merge of main (`a1e1823967`, main parent `8977b13a1c`).

## Claims

- Validate fresh host-local GPU-to-NUMA topology in the launcher, then pass the decision and mapping to children. Preserve constrained CPU affinity and existing non-default memory policies in automatic mode.
- Automatically prefer GPU-local memory with `--preferred`; EngineCore uses `--preferred-many` for multi-node shards. Explicit `--numa-bind` or binding lists retain `--membind`. Failed automatic policy probes fall back to CPU-only, then unbound.
- Enable automatic binding for supported local PCP launches. GPU offsets include TP × PCP × PP for each DP shard, and EngineCore's CPU affinity covers its workers.
- Explicit NUMA CLI flags, including binding-list shortcuts, select `spawn` even when `fork` was requested. Omitted flags and `--no-numa-bind` leave start-method selection unchanged.

## Validation

**CI worker-import fix, 2026-10-27 (`aeef060224`):** The new PCP regression failed in CI because spawned workers could not import its `tests` extension. The test now prepends the checkout root to the server’s `PYTHONPATH`, preserving existing entries. A fresh-worker import reproducer fails without the root and succeeds with it; all applicable pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed. The macOS GPU test skipped for unavailable NVIDIA hardware. `/ci retry` was requested for the failed jobs.

**PCP follow-up, 2026-10-27 (`c9ba84b070`):** 266 targeted local tests passed in 41.39s using the repository's shared fixtures. All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, and `git diff --check` passed.

```bash
env -u UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS= \
  PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 ../vllm-upstream-kv-metrics/.venv/bin/python \
  -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider \
  tests/utils_/test_numa_utils.py tests/utils_/test_system_utils.py \
  tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py tests/v1/executor/test_vllm_net_devices.py \
  -q --tb=short
# 266 passed in 41.39s
```

The new serving regression was run on four B200s with `DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat`, BF16, TP=1, PCP=2, DP=2, local `mp`/`spawn`, MRV2 and eager execution. All four allocated GPUs were on NUMA node 0 of a dual-NUMA host.

Before, on published base `a1e1823967` with the new regression added and the PCP exclusion retained:

```bash
VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
  --tb=short tests/v1/distributed/test_dense_dp_world_size.py::test_pcp_dp_with_auto_numa
# assert parallel.numa_bind and parallel._numa_bind_auto
# 1 failed in 72.68s — workers were unbound
```

After, with the exclusion removed:

```bash
VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
  --tb=short tests/v1/distributed/test_dense_dp_world_size.py::test_pcp_dp_with_auto_numa
# 1 passed in 72.45s — zero skips
```

Both runs generated `' 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5.'`. The passing run verified four distinct GPU UUIDs, GPU indices 0–3, every DP/PCP rank pair, actual `preferred` memory policy, GPU-local CPU affinity `0-31,64-95`, and EngineCore affinity covering each worker. The regression is collected by the existing optional four-L4 distributed CI step. The four-B200 results above come from separate hardware validation; an ineligible-host skip is not successful NUMA validation. The macOS invocation skipped for missing NVIDIA hardware.

A separate ready PCP2/DP2 canary and a NUMA-disabled comparison each completed a nonempty 512-token SSE with `[DONE]`, cached-prompt logprobs, and 80 requests (16 at concurrency 8, 64 at concurrency 32). Each produced 26 complete, schema-valid constrained JSON responses alongside four ordinary requests. Receipt arithmetic, retrieval and generated-code semantic checks failed in both modes; isolated greedy requests pinned to the same DP shard returned identical answers for all three. These results establish the exercised serving behavior, not general model accuracy.

The pod UID, eight worker PIDs and four EngineCore PIDs stayed unchanged, with zero new restarts or OOM events. Both steady-state logs had no tracebacks, engine deaths, CUDA/NCCL errors or grammar rejections. `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` was enabled. CPU offload was disabled; GPU KV capacity was 2 GiB per worker. The disabled comparison used GPU memory utilization 0.8 to coexist with the bound canary; the fixed KV capacity was identical.

Runtime: editable PR Python sources in `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:a7deff2c216def98c193352aca50fb03a2ee29231355b3033dc3789009f6d23e`, with cu130 native artifacts from main `8977b13a1c` and Torch `2.14.0+cu130`. Four unloaded-GPU grammar/CUDA-mask/greedy-sampler preflights passed before loading. Fixture teardown emitted unreaped-process warnings in both regression versions; GPU memory was released and the corrected regression passed. Complete evidence is retained locally.

<details>
<summary>Earlier H200/B200 validation, with tested revisions</summary>

- **2026-10-14:** H200 KV-offload regression passed in 48.82s, zero skips. Python `34a1511ecc` plus the test refinements committed as `2c535797ed`, native artifacts from main `775fefa804ca`; Qwen3-0.6B/BF16, TP=1, MRV2/eager, 128 MiB GPU KV and 256 MiB CPU pool. Worker and EngineCore used `--preferred=0`; 16 blocks completed CPU-to-GPU reload after resetting only the GPU prefix cache, with matching generated token IDs.
- **2026-10-15:** Both explicit binding-list startup cases passed with `fork` preset: nodes selected `spawn` and `MPOL_BIND` with CPUs `0-31,64-95`; explicit CPUs selected `spawn` and `MPOL_BIND` with CPUs `0-7`. Python `2c535797ed` plus the exact fix committed as `40a39f5c40`, using the same image/native base.
- **2026-10-21:** Exact PR Python `40a39f5c404103c351c68d35dcd280ea0a0ace4f`, pinned image above and cu130 artifacts from main `775fefa804ca`. Qwen3-0.6B/BF16, TP=1, `mp`/`spawn`, MRV2/eager, prefix caching, 2 GiB GPU KV and eager SimpleCPUOffloadConnector:

| Case | Observed result |
|---|---|
| Restricted CPU affinity, B200 | CPUs `0-7` preserved; automatic binding disabled; serving succeeded. |
| Inherited `--membind=0`, H200 | Existing `MPOL_BIND` preserved; automatic binding disabled. |
| Denied NUMA syscalls, H200 | Real seccomp `EPERM` for `get_mempolicy`, `set_mempolicy`, `mbind`; automatic binding disabled; serving succeeded. |
| 8 GiB container, 256 MiB CPU offload | Soft preference engaged; peak RAM 3.96 GiB versus 3.97 GiB with binding disabled; neither OOMed. |
| 8 GiB container, 16 GiB CPU offload | Both automatic and disabled modes were OOMKilled before readiness, without early capacity rejection. |

The five surviving canaries completed 512-token SSE, cached-prompt logprobs, tool calls/roundtrips, 400 load requests and 130 shape-valid constrained JSON responses. Each completed CPU-to-GPU restores (80–159 blocks), with unchanged pod UIDs and worker PIDs and zero new restarts. This validated exercised offload behavior, not production capacity. The oversized allocation exposes the existing allocator's admission gap: the allocator matched main `775fefa804ca`, and both NUMA modes attempted the over-limit allocation.

The KV-offload regression is selected by the non-optional NVIDIA `v1-kv-offload` CI step:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_integration.py::test_simple_cpu_offload_with_auto_numa
```

</details>

## Details

| Control | Memory policy |
|---|---|
| Omitted (`numa_bind=None`) | Best-effort soft preference; failed eligibility checks or an existing non-default memory policy mean no vLLM-added binding. |
| `--numa-bind` | Strict `--membind`; missing numactl or undetectable topology remains an error. Existing policy-probe fallback applies. |
| `--no-numa-bind` | No vLLM-added binding. |
| `--numa-bind-nodes` / `--numa-bind-cpus` | Imply explicit enablement and strict memory policy. Combining with `--no-numa-bind` is rejected. |

An internal flag preserves automatic-policy identity after `numa_bind` resolves to `True`, so spawned workers do not mistake it for explicit strict binding. This launch-local state is excluded from the DP configuration hash; no public flag or steady-state inference operation is added.

Automatic eligibility requires CUDA/ROCm, multiple NUMA nodes, numactl and usable memory-policy support, known unrestricted CPU affinity, a default memory policy, and `spawn` with an `mp`/`uni` executor and `mp` DP, including supported PCP launches. Ray, external/custom launchers, device-ID remapping and fork remain excluded. Each launcher interprets NUMA IDs on its own host. The temporary PCP exclusion is removed now that the merged indexing prerequisite and actual bound PCP+DP launches have been verified.

Soft preference permits allocations on other allowed NUMA nodes when local memory is unavailable. Explicit strict binding still needs sufficient memory on the selected nodes. Existing loader RAM estimates and container limits are unchanged; policy probes check acceptance, not allocation capacity.

Unit coverage includes worker/EngineCore policies, fallback, config-copy/hash stability, PCT CPU selection, inherited policies, topology eligibility, CLI start-method selection and PCP/DP indexing. Existing NVIDIA/AMD `utils_` CI retains unit coverage. AMD/ROCm serving, native macOS runtime, hard `cpuset.mems` restrictions, mixed-socket PCP, multi-host PCP and actual preferred-memory spillover remain untested. No throughput or production offload-capacity claim is made. Remote CI build [#97587](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97587) exercised the PCP follow-up; its worker-import failure is addressed by `aeef060224`, with a retry requested.

Duplicate-work searches on 2026-10-15 found no competing upstream GPU automatic-default PR. This PR continues the credited fork trial; other NUMA work addressed affinity, memory sizing, CPU execution or ROCm packaging.
